q: Had I known about the storm, I ___ the trip.
explain: Inverted third conditional: Had I known… = If I had known…, would have + p.p.

q: The bridge is thought ___ over 500 years ago.
explain: Passive reporting about the past: is thought + to have been + p.p.
would rather + someone + past simple for present/future preferences.

q: By next summer, they ___ the new castle.
explain: Future perfect: completed before a future time.

q: The swans, ___ feathers shimmered, glided past.
He must ___ the wrong path; he's still not here.
explain: must have + p.p. = deduction about the past.

q: I'm not used to ___ so much attention.
She'd have won the race if she ___ fallen.
___ by the long journey, the knight fell asleep.
explain: Past participle clause = 'Because he was exhausted…'

q: You ___ have brought a gift, but it's very kind of you.
explain: needn't have + p.p. = you did it, but it wasn't necessary.

q: She's one of the few people ___ can solve the riddle.
I regret ___ you that the boat has sunk.
explain: regret to tell/inform = formal bad news now; regret telling = sorry about the past.

q: The more you practise, ___ you become.
Not until the lake froze ___ how cold it was.
explain: After 'Not until…' at the start, invert: did we realise.
